_comment_shape: Standard CLIF site config. site_name / clif_version / data_directory / filetype / timezone are the consortium-standard keys; the last three are the names clifpy itself requires, so this file is passed to clifpy with no translation layer. Everything below them is this project's protocol.
_comment_versions: clif_version is always the CLIF SPEC version (e.g. 2.1.0). A conversion/ETL release -- the MIMIC-to-CLIF build 1.1.0, say -- is NOT a CLIF version and goes in dataset_version. Leave dataset_version empty for a site's own tables.
_comment_medications: Confirm these against your data before running; vocabularies differ between sources. Phase 0 asserts them and prints the med_category values it actually found, so a mismatch fails loudly rather than producing an empty cohort.
_comment_covariates: Covariate aggregation and missingness rules are PROTOCOL and live in config/covariates.json, which IS tracked in git. This file is not tracked (it carries local paths), so nothing estimand-defining may live here alone.
_comment_protocol: cohort / outcomes / model define the estimand. If two sites set these differently the pooled result is not meaningful -- do not edit them to make a run work.

cohort._comment_anchor: CLIF has no intubation event -- only device_category transitions -- so the anchor is the start of the first continuous IMV episode, which is a PROXY for intubation. A patient transferred in already ventilated, or admitted with a tracheostomy, has hour 0 = first observation rather than start of ventilation. Report and state that.
cohort._comment_imv_episode: imv_episode_gap_hours defines when consecutive IMV records belong to different episodes. 6h is set from the data, not by convention: raw IMV inter-record gaps at UCMC are p50 1.00h, p75 3.33h, p90 4.37h, p95 5.00h, so 14.6% of NORMAL charting gaps exceed 4h and a 4h break would fragment continuously-ventilated patients. At 6h only 2.65% of gaps break an episode. min_imv_hours is separate and is deliberately window_hours: a block that cannot fill one analysis window has no trajectory to model.
cohort._comment_extended_grid: DECLARED BUT NOT CONSUMED. No code reads the two extended_* keys; see covariates.json windows.extended._STATUS for why the 12h/168h view is deferred and what building it would take. Left here so the agreed parameters survive, NOT because a run honours them.

outcomes._comment_mortality: patient.death_dttm is unstable across CLIF sites -- use discharge_category. Sensitivity analysis drops Hospice.

model._comment_scaling: scaling MUST be 0 -- within-unit normalisation erases absolute dose level. See docs/design_notes.md section 3.
model._comment_ng_range: Inclusive [min, max] number of trajectory groups the Phase 3 sweep fits. Lower bound is 2, not 1: a one-group model has no classes to compare and no APPA, OCC or entropy to evaluate. Upper bound 5 (SG, 2026-09-08) -- dBIC was already flattening 43k -> 16k -> 7.7k by ng=5, which is enough to read an elbow; section 7 selects on the elbow, not the global minimum.
model._comment_min_exposed_windows: Phase 3 fits trajectory classes among episodes that received ANY fentanyl inside [0, T]. Episodes with zero dose in every window are held out as a NAMED STRATUM, not modelled as a class: their within-group variance is exactly zero, which makes the Gaussian mixture likelihood unbounded and the IC comparison invalid across ng. MEASURED at UCMC 2026-09-08: with them in, AIC/BIC flipped sign between ng=3 and ng=4 (+1,097,565 to -311,611) as the model isolated the 932 all-zero episodes into a zero-variance component. Threshold is 1: SG 2026-09-08, to maximise n. Raising it to 2 or 3 would drop 490 and 912 episodes respectively.
